newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serb war crimes suspect said to have had stroke.
newsitem.headline: Serb war crimes suspect said to have had stroke.

text.p: The Bosnian Serb government alleged on Friday that war crimes suspect Milan Kovacevic had suffered a stroke in the custody of the U.N. war crimes tribunal in the Netherlands.
A statement said he should be released or examined by Bosnian Serb doctors "because we do not believe the findings of the prison doctors will be objective and professional."
In The Hague, the tribunal confirmed Kovacevic was undergoing tests by Dutch doctors but declined to give details of his ailment.
In a brief statement it said that because of the tests a date would not be set for his initial appearance before the tribunal until July 28 at the earliest.
At the request of his lawyer, Igor Pantelic, medical experts from Belgrade will also be allowed to examine the prisoner.
The Bosnian Serb government assertion, carried by its news agency SRNA, said Kovacevic suffered the stroke on Thursday.
Kovacevic, director of a Bosnian Serb hospital at Prijedor in northwest Bosnia, was arrested last week by British troops after being indicted by the court for complicity in genocide.
The charge stemmed from the ethnic cleansing of Moslems and Croats in north Bosnia at the start of the war in 1992.
Suspects usually make an initial appearance before the tribunal to plead guilty or not guilty within days of their arrest and transfer to The Hague.
